The case of prosecution in brief is that on 17.04.2014 at 02.30 PM, at Mathura Road, Near Okhla Tank bus stand, side from Ashram to Badarpur, New Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Sarita Vihar, the Accused was driving a Eicher Canter/Truck bearing No. HR 29 V 0337 in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and personal safety of others and while so driving Accused person has hit against a rehdi rickshaw being pulled by Govinda Ram and caused grievous injury to him and thereby committed the offences punishable under section 279/338 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter, "IPC"), for which the present FIR was lodged in PS Sarita Vihar.

5. During the course of trial, witnesses namely Dr. H. Raja and Dr. G. Suthakar were dropped from the list of witnesses, pursuant to the statement of the Accused recorded u/s 294 CrPC.
6. Further, since the presence of the injured Govinda Ram, eye witness Sanjay Goswami could not be procured even through DCP concerned, they were dropped from the list of witnesses.
7. PW-1/Nand Kishore has deposed that he was the registered owner of the offending vehicle and that according to him at the time of the accident, the vehicle was being driven by the Accused.
In his cross examination, he admitted that he has not seen the accident and that he was informed of the accident by the Accused.
8. PW-2/T.U. Siddiqui proved the mechanical inspection report Ex. PW2/A and Ex. PW2/B.
No substantial cross examination of PW-2 was conducted.

9. PW-3/HC Vijay Kumar proved the registration of FIR Ex. PW3/A and endorsement on rukka Ex.
PW3/B.
He was not cross examined despite opportunity.
ASI Pooranmal proved the recording of DD No. 28A, Ex. PW4/A.
No substantial cross examination of PW-4 was conducted.

3 11.
PW-5/Sh. Om Parkash deposed that he is working with health department, SDMC.
Their Zonal office (Central Zone) is at Lajpat Nagar, Jal Vihar, New Delhi.
On 18.04.2014, he was going from Lajpat Nagar office to Jaitpur on his motorcycle.
At about 02:30 p.m. when PW-5 reached near Okhla Tank bus stop, he saw a TATA 407 Tempo bearing no. HR-29B-337 which was being driven on the left side of the road.
His motorcycle was on the right side of the tempo as PW-5 was in the process of overtaking the said tempo.

Meanwhile, the driver of said tempo lost control over the vehicle and the tempo climbed over the pavement on the left side of the road and when it was being brought down from the pavement by driver, it hit against a rickshaw rehari from its back side.
The rickshaw rehari got damaged and its rider fell down on the road.
The tempo driver fled away from the spot.
PW-5 immediately called at number 100.
PW-5 chased the tempo on his motorcycle.
The tempo driver drove the truck at a fast speed and stopped his vehicle on wide road.
The driver parked the vehicle on the extreme left side of the road and fled away.
PW-5 identified the tempo.
PW-5 again called PCR and informed about the location of offending vehicle.
PW-5 found one PCR vehicle nearby and informed them about the offending vehicle.
Thereafter, PW-5 left for his work.
PW-5 told the PCR officials that he was ready to get his statement recorded.
PW-5 was never called to PS.
In his cross examination by Ld. APP for the state, PW-5 admitted that he had told the police officials that he can identify the Accused driver of offending vehicle.
PW-5 voluntarily deposed that the face of Accused was fresh in his mind at that point of time.
PW-5 admitted that he had visited the PS on the next day of aforesaid accident.
PW-5 denied the suggestion that he had identified one person as driver of offending vehicle in the PS in the presence of IO.
PW-5 correctly identified the offending tempo.
PW-5 also deposed that he can not identify the Accused.
The driver had driven his tempo at a high speed after causing the aforesaid accident and he could not see him.

Upon confronting with the Accused, PW-5 was asked that whether Accused person was driving the abovesaid vehicle at the time of incident to which PW-5 replied that while he had seen the Accused person shown to him, he cannot say whether he was driving the abovesaid vehicle at the abovesaid time and place or not.
PW-5 was not cross examined despite opportunity.

12. PW-6/HC Ram Vilas deposed that he was posted as HC in PCR Van Kite 72 in the area of PS Sarita Vihar, when he was standing at Madanpur Khadar, one person came on motor cycle to him and informed that one Tempo make Eicher had committed an accident by hitting a rehdi vendor and he followed him, however, he stopped the tempo near Sarita Vihar flyover and ran away from there after leaving the said tempo.
Thereafter, PW-6 informed the DO of PS Sarita Vihar and also to the control room about the accident.
In his cross examination, PW-6 admitted that he is not the witness of the accident and deposed that he does not know whether any TSR or tempo used to stationed near the Sarita Vihar flyover.
PW- 6 denied the suggestion that he is deposing falsely at the behest of the IO or that such incident had taken place.
13. PW-7/Retd.
SI Malkhan Singh deposed that on 17.04.2014, PW-7 was posted at PS Sarita Vihar as SI.

On that day, after receiving DD No. 28A, PW-7 alongwith Ct. Pooran reached the spot, i.e.,
Mathura road, near Okhla tank bus stand.

After reaching the spot, PW-7 saw a rehdi rickshaw in an State vs Ravi Singh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3826950/
4
accidental condition.
On enquiry, PW-7 came to know that injured has already been shifted to hospital.
At that time, PW-7 received DD Number with regard to admission of the injured at Apollo hospital.
Thereafter, PW-7 went to Apollo hospital and collected MLC of the injured namely Govinda.
However, the injured was not in a condition to give a statement.

Thereafter, PW-7 received another DD with regard to the presence of offending vehicle, i.e., vehicle bearing registration No.
HR 29 V 0337 at F Block, Sarita Vihar.
PW-7 immediately reached the spot, thereafter, PW-7 saw the offending vehicle parked and there was fresh damage seen on the said vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not found.
Thereafter, PW-7 seized the offending vehicle vide seizure memo Ex. PW7/A.
PW-7 also seized the rehdi rickshaw vide seizure memo Ex. PW7/B.
Thereafter, PW-7 came to the PS and deposit the vehicles at malkhana.
PW-7 also prepared the site plan of the spot which is Ex. PW7/C. PW-7 also recorded the statement of the witnesses.

Thereafter, on 18.04.2014,
PW-7 gave notice u/s 133 MV Act to RC owner.
Thereafter, he came to the PS alongwith Accused driver namely Ravi Singh.
He also produced the photocopy of the documents of the offending vehicle and PW-7 seized the same vide seizure memo Ex. PW7/D.

Thereafter, PW-7 seized the DL of the Accused Ex. PW7/E. Nand Kishore produced invoice with regard to proof of delivery with regard to the offending vehicle and the same was seized vide seizure memo Ex. PW7/F.
Thereafter, PW-7 arrested Accused vide arrest memo Ex. PW7/G and conducted his personal search vide Ex. PW7/H.
Thereafter, Accused was released on police bail.
Thereafter, PW-7 recorded the statement of the injured.
During the investigation, PW-7 got conducted the mechanical inspection of the vehicles.
Thereafter, PW-7 prepared chargesheet and filed before the Hon'ble court.
PW-7 correctly identified the Accused and offending vehicle, the rehdi rickshaw and spot of incident in court.
The photographs are already Ex. P-1 to Ex. P-15.
In his cross examination, PW-7 deposed that he did not find any eye witness at the spot when he reached for the first time.

PW-7 denied the suggestion that the accident was not caused by the offending vehicle and the Accused has been falsely implicated in the present case in order to get compensation from MACT and that the mechanical inspection was not conducted in a fair manner.
STATEMENT OF ACCUSED 14.

Thereafter, before the start of defence evidence, in order to allow the Accused to personally explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against him, the statement of Accused was recorded without oath on 16.10.2023 under section 313 CrPC in which he stated that he is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.

He further stated that he did not wish to lead DE.
ARGUMENTS AND ANALYSIS 15.
I have heard the Ld. APP for the state and Ld. counsel for the Accused at length.
I have also given my thoughtful consideration to the material appearing on record.
16. It is argued by the Ld. APP for the state that there is sufficient material on record to convict the Accused for the said offences.

State vs Ravi Singh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3826950/
5 17.
Per contra, the Ld. Counsel for the Accused has argued that the state has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt.

Ld. Counsel has argued that the Accused has not been identified by the eye witness and that the injured never came to court to depose as part of the prosecution evidence and hence the Accused deserves to be acquitted.
18.
The Accused person has been charged for the offences under section 279/338 IPC.
Needless to mention, in criminal law, the burden of proof on the prosecution is that of beyond a reasonable doubt.
The presumption of innocence of the Accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by reducing cogent evidence that points towards the guilt of the Accused.
The evidence in the present case is to be weighed keeping in view the above legal standards.
20. The first ingredient in itself has not been proved in the present case.
The fact that the offending vehicle was being driven on a public way is proved from the testimony of PW-5.

However, the fact that the Accused was driving the offending vehicle is not proved beyond all reasonable doubt, as firstly the main victim/injured did not come before the court and was dropped from the list of witnesses, secondly, even the second eye witness Sh. Sanjay Goswami was dropped from the list of witnesses as he did not appear for his testimony.

The only eye witness to the incident, whose testimony is on record, i.e., PW-5, has failed to identify the Accused as the driver of the offending vehicle, even after cross examination by Ld. APP for the state.

While PW-1/the superdar of offending vehicle has stated that as per him, the offending vehicle was being driven by the Accused,
he has admittedly not seen the accident and his evidence is only hearsay and at the maximum proves that the offending vehicle may have been under the custody of the Accused but cannot conclusively prove that the same was being driven by the Accused.
There is no CCTV footage of the incident and even the TIP of the Accused was never conducted and the Accused was not arrested at the spot but has only been arrested later on 18.04.2014.

In these circumstances, since the ingredients of the offences are cumulative in nature and the first ingredient itself, i.e., whether the Accused was driving the offending vehicle or not is not proved, no useful purpose would be served by discussing the remaining ingredients of the offences.

21. Furthermore, it has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dr. S.L. Goswami vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 197 SCC (Crl.) 258 that the Accused persons are entitled to benefit of doubt where the onus of proving the ingredients of the offence is not discharged by the prosecution.

6 present case, as already noted above, the prosecution could not discharge the onus of proving the ingredients of offences in question and thus, the Accused person is entitled to benefit of doubt.
22.
Hence, it has not been proved that the offending vehicle was being driven by the Accused.
To recapitulate the above discussion, to bring home the guilt of Accused person, the prosecution was required to prove the offence under section 279/338 IPC beyond reasonable doubt.
There is no evidence to suggest that the Accused was driving the offending vehicle.
Further, the ingredients of the offence are not fulfilled from the material on record.

In the present case, as already noted above,
the prosecution could not discharge the onus of proving the ingredients of offences in question and thus, the Accused person is entitled to benefit of doubt.
23.
Resultantly, the Accused person namely, RAVI SINGH, S/o Sh. HAKIM SINGH is hereby found not guilty.

He is hereby ACQUITTED of the offences under section 279/338 IPC.
24.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
Announced in open court on 15.12.2023 in the presence of the Accused.
